title: When Ron Went to the Ohel

article.body:

“I’m so glad to see you!” Ron exclaimed. “I knew you were coming to New York at the same time as me, so I waited for you. Let’s go to the Ohel again!”

“But I wasn’t planning on going this time,” Zeidy blurted out. “Why do you want to go so badly?"

With a voice filled with emotion, Ron replied: "Last time you took me to the Ohel, I asked the Rebbe for three things: First, to heal my stomach pains. Second, to help me keep my job at Hughes Aircraft. And third, to show me where to live, because California was getting too expensive.

“I had never gone to the Ohel before, so I was wondering if my prayers would help,” Ron continued. “Well, I didn’t have to wait long to find out! As soon as I arrived back home, I got an offer to work for Hughes Aircraft in Texas, where the cost of living is much cheaper. And shortly after that, my stomach pains started to go away. Everything I asked for

Ron’s story, he was overwhelmed with emotion. If the Rebbe took

care of Ron, who isn’t even Jewish, how much more so for us chassidim! he realized with wonder. How lucky we are to be chassidim of the Rebbe!

When a non-Jewish man visited the Ohel, Zeidy learned a powerful lesson. How lucky we are to be the Rebbe’s chassidim!

Our Zeidy worked at Hughes Aircraft in California for many years. Because of his job, he had to travel to New York many times throughout the year.

Once, while relaxing on his flight to New York, Zeidy felt a tap on his shoulder. It was Ron, another man who worked at Zeidy’s company.

“Good to see you, Mr. Plotke!” Ron said happily. “I would love to have someone to talk to during the boring ride to the hotel. Let’s go together!”

Zeidy politely shook his head. “I don’t think it will work,” he explained to Ron, who wasn’t Jewish. “I’m stopping at the Lubavitcher Rebbe’s Ohel on my way to the hotel.”

“Oh, that sounds cool!” Ron exclaimed. “I also want to go!”

Zeidy hesitated, unsure of what to do. Ron isn’t Jewish. Should I bring him along? But when he saw Ron’s excitement, he agreed to take him.

As they left the airport, they bumped into an Israeli businessman. “Rabbi, are you by any chance going to the Ohel?” he asked.

“Indeed we are!” answered Zeidy. “Come, join our ride.”

As they rode together, the businessman told Ron about the Rebbe. “The Rebbe is the leader of our generation,” he explained. “People from all over the world come to pray at the Ohel, and the Rebbe helps them!”

Ron listened in wonder. “But what about me?” he asked. “I’m not Jewish. Can I also pray at the Ohel?”

“Of course!” the businessman replied. When they arrived, Ron wrote a letter to the Rebbe and went inside the Ohel to ask for the things he needed.
